concepts.title: $K_0$ of a ring: the Grothendieck group of projective modules
concepts.blurb: $K_0(R)$ is the Grothendieck group of finitely generated projective $R$-modules under direct sum: free abelian on isomorphism classes $[P]$ modulo $[P\oplus Q]=[P]+[Q]$. Two projectives represent the same class iff they become isomorphic after stabilizing by a free summand: $[P]=[Q]$ iff $P\oplus R^n\cong Q\oplus R^n$ for some $n$. For a field, $K_0(R)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ records rank; for a Dedekind domain, $K_0(R)\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathrm{Cl}(R)$ adds the ideal class group. The same construction recovers vector bundles on a space, locally free sheaves on a scheme, and the class group in number theory under one umbrella.

concepts.title: $K_1$ of a ring: stable invertible matrices
concepts.blurb: $K_1(R)$ is the abelianization of the stable general linear group $GL(R)=\varinjlim GL_n(R)$ — invertible matrices of all sizes glued along the upper-left embedding. Whitehead's lemma identifies the commutator subgroup $[GL(R),GL(R)]$ with the elementary subgroup $E(R)$ generated by transvections $I+r\,e_{ij}$, so $K_1(R)=GL(R)/E(R)$. For commutative $R$ the determinant splits the surjection $K_1(R)\twoheadrightarrow R^\times$, leaving $SK_1(R)$ as the genuinely new content; for fields $SK_1(F)=0$ so $K_1(F)=F^\times$ exactly, and Bass-Milnor-Serre proves $SK_1$ also vanishes for Dedekind domains. The Whitehead group $\mathrm{Wh}(G)=K_1(\mathbb{Z}[G])/(\pm G^{\mathrm{ab}})$ houses Reidemeister torsion and the s-cobordism obstruction in surgery theory — a direct geometric payload built from $K_1$ of an integral group ring.

concepts.title: $K_2$ of a ring and the Steinberg relations
concepts.blurb: $K_2(R)$ is the kernel of the universal central extension $\mathrm{St}(R)\twoheadrightarrow E(R)$. The Steinberg group $\mathrm{St}(R)$ has generators $x_{ij}(r)$ — abstract avatars of the elementary matrices $I+r\,e_{ij}$ — subject only to commutator relations encoding row operations; its abstract centre measures hidden relations among elementary matrices that aren't forced by the row-operation rules. For a field $F$, Matsumoto's theorem identifies $K_2(F)$ with symbols $\{a,b\}$ on $F^\times\otimes F^\times$ modulo bilinearity and the Steinberg relation $\{a,1-a\}=1$. Concrete computations: $K_2(\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}/2$ generated by $\{-1,-1\}$ (Tate); $K_2(\mathbb{F}_q)=0$ (Quillen). The tame-symbol map $K_2(\mathbb{Q})\to\bigoplus_p\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ encodes quadratic reciprocity as a single $K_2$-relation, and Merkurjev-Suslin links $K_2(F)/n$ to the Brauer group via norm-residue symbols.

concepts.title: Quillen's Q-construction and higher K-theory
concepts.blurb: Quillen defined $K_n(R)=\pi_{n+1}(BQ\mathcal{P}(R))$, where $\mathcal{P}(R)$ is the exact category of finitely generated projective $R$-modules and $Q\mathcal{P}$ is the combinatorial Q-construction whose morphisms are zigzags of admissible epi-then-mono. The shift by one is structural: $\pi_1(BQ\mathcal{P})\cong K_0(\mathcal{P})$, so a single space carries $K_0,K_1,K_2,\ldots$ in adjacent homotopy degrees. The construction extends verbatim to any exact category: $K_n(\mathcal{E})=\pi_{n+1}BQ\mathcal{E}$. Two equivalent definitions exist: Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$-construction for categories with cofibrations and weak equivalences (extending K-theory to chain complexes and stable $\infty$-categories), and the plus-construction $K_n(R)=\pi_n(BGL(R)^+)$ for $n\ge 1$. Quillen's plus-equals-Q theorem reconciles them — three definitions, one homotopy invariant — and feeds the localization theorem and motivic spectral sequences downstream.

concepts.title: The localization long exact sequence
concepts.blurb: For a ring $R$ and a multiplicative subset $S$, Quillen's localization theorem produces a long exact sequence $\cdots\to K_{n+1}(S^{-1}R)\to K_n(\mathcal{H}_S(R))\to K_n(R)\to K_n(S^{-1}R)\to\cdots$, where $\mathcal{H}_S(R)$ is the category of finitely generated $S$-torsion $R$-modules of finite Tor-dimension. This is the engine that makes higher K-theory computable: the connecting maps are residue maps recording boundary behaviour of K-classes under inverting $S$. Applied to $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$, the residue maps $K_n(\mathbb{Q})\to\bigoplus_p K_{n-1}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ (one per prime) reduce $K_*(\mathbb{Z})$ to Quillen's calculation of $K_*(\mathbb{F}_p)$, recovering $K_2(\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Z}/2$ and Borel's rational ranks tied to special values of the Dedekind zeta function. The same machinery underlies the Gersten resolution and the spectral sequence from local-to-global K-theory of schemes.

concepts.title: Applications: Bass-Quillen, Wall finiteness, motivic K-theory
concepts.blurb: K-theory underwrites three flagship results. The Bass-Quillen theorem (Serre's conjecture for regular rings) says every finitely generated projective $R[t]$-module extends from $R$ when $R$ is regular Noetherian — proven via $K_0$-theoretic patching. Wall's finiteness obstruction lives in $\widetilde{K}_0(\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1 X])$: a finitely dominated CW complex is homotopy equivalent to a finite one iff this class vanishes. Motivic K-theory, the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum picture proven through Voevodsky's work on the Bloch-Kato conjecture, computes algebraic K-theory of smooth varieties via motivic cohomology — a deep bridge from ring-theoretic invariants to arithmetic geometry.
